inspection_summary: Inspected all 912 assignment-aligned lines of Habsieger's article. The source recasts the Nyman-Beurling closure condition inside a symmetry-defined Hilbert subspace with an explicit Fourier-equivalent orthonormal basis, computes coordinates of the fractional-part generators, and develops triangular, natural, and smoothed Möbius-weighted approximation schemes. Each scheme has the required coordinatewise limit and an automatic far-tail estimate, while RH remains conditional on finding a single square-summable coordinate envelope over the unresolved intermediate range. Formula extraction is imperfect but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose and adjacent displayed formulas; exact symbolic reuse should be checked against the retained PDF.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the Nyman-Beurling density problem, the symmetry-adapted orthonormal family, and the three approximation programs.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the closure formulations equivalent to RH and previews the coordinatewise-plus-domination strategy.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Orthonormality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs the sine-difference family, proves orthonormality, characterizes its closed span by periodicity and reflection antisymmetry, and identifies it with an odd-cosine Fourier subspace.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Density results and the Riemann hypothesis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves dilation completeness and transfers the Nyman-Beurling criterion to density of the generators e_q in the symmetry subspace.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Computational lemmas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes generator coordinates and pairwise scalar products, then isolates the Möbius-sum inputs used by all later approximations.

sections_inspected.label: 5. The triangular approximation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Solves a finite triangular coordinate-matching problem, gives its exact residual tail, proves a remote-tail estimate, and states the remaining square-summable domination criterion.

sections_inspected.label: 6. The natural approximation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Studies the uncorrected Möbius-weighted approximant, derives coordinate limits and tail control, and quantifies a low-coordinate mass obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Smooth approximations and acknowledgements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces exponent smoothing, proves its coordinate limits and tail estimate under a decay window, and states the corresponding RH criterion and conditional comparison.

sections_inspected.label: References and author metadata
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic provenance only; no additional source argument.

accepted_units.title: Nyman-Beurling closure target and symmetry-subspace reformulation
accepted_units.why_material: The article begins from the equivalence between RH and approximation of the indicator of [1,+infinity) by fractional-part functions, then announces the sharper target of approximating E1 by e_q={qt}-{t} inside an explicitly manageable subspace. This fixes the semantic target used by every later construction.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the Hilbert norm and definitions of rho_a, E1, and e_q with the equivalence; the Baez-Duarte integer restriction is reported as prior work by the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on weighted L2 closure and fractional-part notation, but not on the later coordinate formulas.

accepted_units.title: Coordinate convergence plus square-summable domination
accepted_units.why_material: The source isolates the decisive proof architecture: compute basis coordinates, show each tends to the target coordinate, and seek a subsequence with a uniform square-summable envelope so dominated convergence yields norm convergence. The three later criteria differ mainly in where this envelope is still needed.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a strategy statement, not evidence that any of the proposed envelopes exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the orthonormal-basis representation introduced in the surrounding paper outline; the logic is an l2 domination argument.

accepted_units.title: Sine-difference orthonormal family
accepted_units.why_material: Defining E_n as consecutive differences of sine waves turns the integral kernel min(p,q) into Kronecker orthogonality. The construction is reusable because a covariance-like min kernel is diagonalized by discrete differences.
accepted_units.context_note: The oscillatory integral lemma and the orthogonality computation are both included so the construction is locally justified.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: exact constants and the weighted integral should be verified against the PDF before symbolic reuse, although the min-kernel cancellation is readable.

accepted_units.title: Symmetry characterization and Fourier model of H_P
accepted_units.why_material: The closed span of the E_n is exactly the weighted-L2 functions that are one-periodic and antisymmetric under x maps to 1-x. A weighted rescaling maps this space isometrically to a subspace of L2(0,1) where the E_n become the standard odd-frequency cosine basis, making completeness and coefficient reasoning transparent.
accepted_units.context_note: The span characterization, norm transformation, induced symmetries, Parseval step, and image basis form one coherent representation change.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly tied to periodic/reflection symmetries and the multiplier pi/(sqrt(2) sin(2 pi x)); exact typography is formula-sensitive but the prose supports the isomorphism.

accepted_units.title: Dilation orbit of E1 is dense in the ambient Hilbert space
accepted_units.why_material: A compactly supported function is encoded into a periodic antisymmetric g_T, expanded in H_P, and then rescaled back to approximate the original function with an explicit vanishing error. This constructively proves density of the dilation span of E1 and contrasts it with a nonconstructive Mellin-Wiener criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed definition at line 227 appears to use x where t is expected, but the construction and convergence argument are otherwise recoverable; check the PDF for exact variable names.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses dilation, periodic folding by fractional parts, H_P completeness, and the weighted L2 norm; the alternative proof uses a Mellin-transform nonvanishing condition.

accepted_units.title: RH as density of e_q in H_P with a coefficient-sum repair
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 transports the standard Nyman-Beurling condition through an isometry to approximation of E1 by {qt} in H, then proves that the common {t} component can be removed. Reflection of the residual controls the sum of coefficients, so adding that small multiple of {t} converts the approximants into finite combinations of e_q without losing convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: Include both directions and the residual estimate; merely quoting the theorem would hide the nontrivial repair from unrestricted fractional-part generators to symmetry-compatible differences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the cited Nyman-Beurling/Baez-Duarte equivalence and cited isometry as source inputs; the coefficient-sum correction is proved locally in the weighted norm.

accepted_units.title: Exact E_p-coordinate of a fractional-part difference
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 2 converts each generator e_q into the explicit coefficient log q minus a short reciprocal sum indexed by p/q <= k < p. This is the computational bridge from functional approximation to arithmetic coordinate estimates used in every subsequent scheme.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof rewrites a weighted sine/fractional-part integral and then takes the consecutive-sine difference defining E_p.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact summation endpoints, floors, and integral constants are formula-dependent and should be checked against the PDF before machine transcription.

accepted_units.title: Generator Gram matrix via Vassiounine sums
accepted_units.why_material: The pairwise inner product of e_p and e_q is expressed through logarithmic terms and Vassiounine cotangent sums, providing an alternative route for norm computations and exposing arithmetic structure beyond individual basis coordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: The result is quoted as following from a prior Vassiounine autocorrelation formula rather than independently derived in full.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-sensitive; the semantic relation to fractional-part autocorrelation is clear, but exact signs, gcd arguments, and constants require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Common domination framework and Möbius-sum inputs
accepted_units.why_material: The paper makes the remaining task explicit: coordinatewise convergence must be supplemented by a uniform square-summable majorant, with only a bounded index window left after far-tail estimates. Rapid logarithmic decay of partial Möbius sums and convergence of their logarithmic weighting to -1 supply the common analytic inputs.
accepted_units.context_note: The Möbius estimates are invoked as consequences of the prime number theorem and partial summation, so they are assumptions established by cited standard results rather than new proofs here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses orthonormal coordinates, l2 dominated convergence, the Möbius function, and harmonic sums.

accepted_units.title: Triangular approximation with an exact residual tail
accepted_units.why_material: The coefficients lambda_{q,n} retain Möbius weights through n-1 and choose two boundary corrections by a two-equation system. The resulting error with E1 has coordinates -1 at p=1, zero for 2<=p<=n before adding E1, and hence vanishes through the first n coordinates, while all residual coefficients p>=n+1 receive an explicit harmonic-sum formula.
accepted_units.context_note: The sign convention is that the displayed finite combination plus E1 equals the residual tail; preserve it when reusing the construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Lemma 2, Möbius divisor cancellation, harmonic sums, and exact boundary-coefficient formulas; verify OCR-sensitive fractions and signs.

accepted_units.title: Remote-tail bound for the triangular residual
accepted_units.why_material: Euler-Maclaurin control and the Möbius-sum estimates give x_{n,p}=O(n^2/(p log n)), hence a square-summable p-dependent bound once p is at least n^4. This confines the unresolved domination problem to the finite moving interval immediately above the matched coordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: The extracted comparison symbol at lines 604-605 is damaged, but the prose explicitly calls it the second estimate and Criterion 1 confirms its role as a bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on the exact residual formula from the preceding unit and on asymptotic big-O estimates; the threshold n^4 is legible.

accepted_units.title: Triangular square-summable-window criterion for RH
accepted_units.why_material: Criterion 1 states that a uniform square-summable envelope only on p in [n+1,n^4] for infinitely many n closes the triangular approximation argument and implies RH. It precisely identifies the scheme's remaining burden after exact low-coordinate cancellation and automatic far-tail control.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a sufficient condition, not a demonstrated estimate or an equivalence established independently of Theorem 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on units u02, u10, and u11 and on interpreting the extracted summability display as sum_p u_p^2<infinity.

accepted_units.title: Natural Möbius approximation: coordinate limits and tail control
accepted_units.why_material: Dropping the two boundary corrections gives the natural coefficients mu(q)/q. Divisor cancellation plus Möbius-sum asymptotics yields coordinatewise convergence to -E1, while a direct generator-coordinate estimate gives y_{n,p}=O(n/p) and automatic domination beyond n^2 log n.
accepted_units.context_note: The target sign is negative: the finite combination's first coordinate tends to -1 and all other fixed coordinates tend to zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Lemmas 2 and 4, Möbius divisor sums, and the E_p basis; the missing comparison glyph at lines 665-666 is recoverable as an upper-bound statement from adjacent prose.

accepted_units.title: Natural-approximation domination criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Criterion 2 reduces RH for the natural approximants to a square-summable uniform coordinate envelope on p up to n^2 log n for infinitely many n. Compared with the triangular scheme the unresolved range is shorter at the top but includes all low coordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: The following proposition shows why inclusion of the low-coordinate range is a serious obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on unit u13 and the coordinate-domination strategy; exact summability notation is formula-sensitive but unambiguous in context.

accepted_units.title: Exact low-coordinate energy exposes restrictive Möbius conditions
accepted_units.why_material: An exact formula for the sum of y_{n,p}^2 over 2<=p<=n+1 converts success of Criterion 2 into simultaneous smallness conditions on two Möbius partial-sum combinations. The source argues these are quite restrictive and contrasts them with known square-root-scale oscillation, diagnosing why coordinatewise convergence alone is inadequate.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed identity is algebraically dense and OCR-sensitive; retain the conceptual conclusion and verify every term against the PDF before computational use. The source says the infinite subsequence seems difficult to find, not impossible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses the explicit low-index coordinate formula, harmonic-sum identities, and asymptotic information on summatory Möbius values.

accepted_units.title: Exponent-smoothed Möbius approximation
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing mu(q)/q by mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), with epsilon_n tending to zero no faster than the stated logarithmic threshold, preserves coordinatewise convergence to -E1 and the O(n/p) far-tail estimate. The proof rewrites divisor sums by Euler products and controls zeta-tail errors directly.
accepted_units.context_note: The extraction renders epsilon as a control character-like glyph, but its role, lower bound 2 log log n/log n, and o(1) condition are clear. Exact exponent typography and tail estimates need PDF verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the basis-coordinate formula, Euler-product identities for 1/zeta and its derivative, and quantitative tail bounds in the smoothing parameter.

accepted_units.title: Smoothed domination criterion and conditional calibration
accepted_units.why_material: Criterion 3 gives the smoothed analogue of Criterion 2: a square-summable envelope through n^2 log n along infinitely many n implies RH. The source reports that under RH prior work verifies the criterion for a particular logarithmic smoothing scale and even bounds the approximation distance, making this scheme a conditional calibration rather than an unconditional proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The final efficiency claim is explicitly conditional on RH and attributed to Balazard; it cannot be used as independent evidence for RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on unit u16 and cited external conditional results; the source's extracted epsilon symbol should be normalized only after scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From semantic symmetry to an arithmetic l2 fertility test
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source turns a weighted functional closure statement into an explicit l2 coefficient problem by selecting the symmetry class naturally containing the fractional-part differences, diagonalizing that class with a Fourier-equivalent basis, and computing each generator's arithmetic coordinates.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The closure-to-RH link uses cited Nyman-Beurling and Baez-Duarte results, and the transformation does not itself supply the missing uniform coordinate envelope.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Three approximation schemes isolate moving domination windows
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Triangular correction, raw Möbius weighting, and exponent smoothing all solve fixed-coordinate convergence and admit automatic remote-tail control; they differ in exact low-coordinate cancellation and in the moving interval on which a common square-summable majorant remains necessary.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: All three RH conclusions are conditional on an unproved domination hypothesis for infinitely many n; coordinatewise limits and big-O tails alone do not give Hilbert-norm convergence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Low-coordinate energy motivates smoothing but does not validate it unconditionally
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The natural scheme's exact low-coordinate energy forces simultaneous cancellation in Möbius partial sums, revealing a concrete obstruction that the smoothed weights are designed to soften while preserving the same target coordinates.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not prove that smoothing removes the unconditional obstruction; its strongest positive efficiency statement assumes RH and cites prior work.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Constructive and transform-based completeness viewpoints
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The article pairs two representation mechanisms: symmetry reduction identifies an explicit Fourier basis for H_P, while periodic folding and dilation reconstruct arbitrary compactly supported functions in H; a Mellin-Wiener criterion supplies a parallel transform explanation of dilation completeness.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Only the periodic-folding proof supplies an explicit approximation rate in the source, and neither completeness result by itself resolves the RH-specific restricted-generator closure.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for source-level semantic planning: all seven mathematical sections were inspected through their proofs, comparisons, and conditional criteria. Every distinct reusable mechanism is represented; unselected lines are connective exposition, repeated coordinate algebra inside represented derivations, page furniture, acknowledgements, or bibliography. OCR-sensitive formulas are retained only where adjacent prose makes their mathematical role recoverable and are flagged for PDF verification.
stop_reason: The source ends after three approximation families have each been reduced to an explicit unresolved square-summable domination window, with the natural family's low-coordinate obstruction and the smoothed family's conditional calibration accounted for. Lines 877-912 contain only references and author metadata, so further segmentation would duplicate represented derivations or select nonmathematical material rather than add a new mechanism.
